scenes.headline: How Invaria keeps point cloud models steady across grids
scenes.sub: Scale fixed by measurement, density learned by predicting the next resolution.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lumen! Train a point cloud model at a two centimetre grid, test it at six, and it falls apart. Here is how Invaria holds on.

scenes.title: Why the grid breaks the usual model

left.title: The usual way
items: Grid size is fixed in the config
A coarser grid looks like a smaller room
left.say: Every kernel inside the usual network counts grid cells. Triple the grid, and to the model the room has shrunk to a third.

right.title: Invaria
items: Shrink the scene, the grid shrinks too
right.say: Invaria measures its grid from the points, and trains on several densities at once.

scenes.text: Measure the grid instead of declaring it, and train the encoder to predict features one resolution finer than it was given.

parts.note: each random anchor to its closest neighbour
parts.say: Measure how far some random anchor points sit from their nearest neighbours, and take the mean.
Scale it by a constant. Shrink the scene, and the grid shrinks with it.

steps.say: In training, the model gets a sparse copy of the scene, and calibrates its grid from it.
A shallower Point Transformer encodes those points.
The predictor adds the points of the next, denser level, and refines features for them.
The loss is segmentation at that finer level, so the model cannot lean on one density.
The paper's own chart. Baselines trained at two centimetres slide down as the grid coarsens.
Invaria stays flat. A Point Transformer retrained at each grid stays just above it.

scenes.label: mIoU at a 6 cm grid, Invaria against the best baseline
scenes.say: At six centimetres, Invaria scores seventy-three point eight against forty-seven point three. That is the abstract's fifty-six percent: relative, not points.

scenes.text: A grid-native network sees cells, not centimetres. Calibration fixes scale by construction; density has to be trained in.

recap: Coarser grid looks like a smaller room
Measure the grid from the points
scenes.say: Measure the grid, train across densities, and a coarser scan stops looking like a smaller room.
